extracted.intended_audience: government officials, legal practitioners, journalists, researchers, and members of the public interested in Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) requirements and advisory committee governance
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and legal requirements governing the creation, operation, transparency, and oversight of federal advisory committees under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA). Useful for officials forming or managing advisory committees and for parties monitoring committee compliance and public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "advisory committee"
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA defines "advisory committee" as "any committee, board, commission, council, conference, panel, task force, or other similar group" that dispenses "advice or recommendations" to the President of the United States, and excludes bodies that also exercise operational functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion determines whether a body falls under FACA's requirements (meeting openness, chartering, reporting). The definition emphasizes groups that provide advice/recommendations rather than operational decision-making. Bodies that exercise operational functions are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: employee-only bodies and specified organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees composed of full-time officers or employees of the federal government do not count as advisory committees under FACA. The Act also does not govern certain organizations (e.g., Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations; Commission on Government Procurement; National Academy of Sciences; Central Intelligence Agency; Federal Reserve; National Academy of Public Administration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these exclusion rules to determine applicability; listing of specific exempted organizations clarifies FACA's scope. When assessing applicability, evaluate membership composition (full-time federal employees vs. nonfederal members).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: objective and accessible advice; formalized lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislators intended to ensure that advice by advisory committees is "objective and accessible to the public" by formalizing the process for "establishing, operating, overseeing, and terminating" the committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normative standard underlies FACA: committees should produce objective advice available to the public and be subject to formal establishment and oversight processes. Committee Management Secretariat (GSA) is charged with monitoring compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on formation, powers, and term
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA restricts the formation of such committees to only those which are deemed essential, limits their powers to provision of advice to officers and agencies in the executive branch, and limits the length of term during which any such committee may operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating or evaluating committees, require justification that the committee is essential, ensure its charter limits it to advisory (not operational) functions, and document/limit the term of operation per statutory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on open meetings, chartering, public involvement, and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act has special emphasis on open meetings, chartering, public involvement, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad transparency and procedural obligations are core to FACA: committees should be chartered, engage public involvement where appropriate, hold open meetings by default, and provide reporting to enable public scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice in the Federal Register (15 days prior and required contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A committee must provide public notice in the Federal Register 15 days prior to holding a meeting. It must publish all information regarding the meeting, including committee name, the time, place, and purpose of the meeting, and a summary of the agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule is specific and mandatory: file notice at least 15 days in advance and include committee name, time, place, purpose, and agenda summary. Failure to provide proper notice may violate FACA transparency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed-meeting notice requirements and Sunshine Act exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If any part of the meeting is closed to the public, the notice must include the committee name; the time, place and purpose of the meeting; a summary of the agenda; and if any portion of the meeting is closed, the reason and exemption(s) in the Government in the Sunshine Act that apply. An advisory committee meeting can be closed to the public if the president or an agency head determines that any of the 10 exemptions to the Sunshine Act apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When closing meetings, explicitly cite the Sunshine Act exemption(s) relied upon and state the reason in the Federal Register notice. The decision to close rests with the president or agency head and must reference one of the statutory exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to committee materials and records; FOIA interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee must provide access to materials provided to it, including reports, transcripts, minutes, working papers, agendas or other documents unless any of the nine FOIA exemptions would apply. The committees must also keep minutes of their meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency requires making documents available to the public except where FOIA exemptions apply; maintain and preserve meeting minutes and other records. When withholding materials, document the applicable FOIA exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing hidden "locker-room" discussions and ensuring public administration of hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA was an attempt by Congress to curtail the "locker-room discussion" practice (meetings masked under titles like "task force", "subcommittee", and "working group") which are less than full FACA meetings and therefore not open to the public; FACA declared that all administrative procedures and hearings were to be public knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether advisory activity is being conducted via subgroups to evade openness obligations; require that substantive deliberations subject to FACA be held in properly noticed meetings and not centralized in informal or unchartered gatherings intended to avoid public scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing duplication and usefulness (GAO recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO reviewed DOT and DOE advisory groups to assess whether department assessment processes help ensure advisory group efforts are not duplicative and to what extent groups are useful; the review resulted in four recommendations geared toward preventing duplication of efforts among FACA groups and enhancing usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrations should implement routine assessments (as envisioned by Sec. 21 of Pub. L. No. 111-139) to identify duplicative committees or efforts and to improve the usefulness of advisory groups. Usefulness and non-duplication are evaluative criteria for continued authorization of committees.
